title: Public-key quantum money from LWE alone
formal: Does quantum hardness of decisional Learning with Errors with the fixed polynomial parameters below imply reusable, unforgeable public-key quantum money in the standard model?
definitions: For each integer \(\lambda\ge2\), let \(q(\lambda)\) be the least prime at least \(\lambda^4\), and let \(\chi_\lambda\) give integer z probability proportional to \(\exp(-\pi z^2/\lambda^2)\). The assumption states that, for every polynomially bounded sample count m, the distributions \((A,As+e\bmod q)\) and \((A,u)\) are computationally indistinguishable: A is uniform in \(\mathbb Z_q^{m\times\lambda}\), s is independently uniform in \(\mathbb Z_q^\lambda\), the coordinates of e are independent samples from \(\chi_\lambda\), and u is independent uniform in \(\mathbb Z_q^m\). Indistinguishability is against all nonuniform polynomial-size quantum circuit families with classical advice. Advantage is the absolute difference of acceptance probabilities and must be negligible in lambda, meaning eventually less than \(\lambda^{-c}\) for every constant c>0. Quantum circuits use a fixed universal Clifford-plus-T gate set, zero-state ancillas and computational-basis measurements; polynomial-size classical control is allowed. A money scheme consists of uniform quantum polynomial-time algorithms Gen, Mint and Verify. Gen on unary lambda outputs classical keys (pk,sk). Mint(sk) outputs a classical serial string s and a quantum register rho; their lengths are polynomial in lambda. Verify(pk,s,rho) returns an accept/reject bit and a residual note register, without secret information. For every polynomial t, an honestly generated note survives t successive verifications, all accepting, with probability at least one minus a negligible function, over key generation, minting and verification. For every polynomially bounded integer-valued k and every nonuniform polynomial-size quantum adversary with classical advice, give the adversary pk and k independently minted notes under the same key. The probability that it produces k+1 serial/register pairs all accepted by fresh local applications of Verify is negligible; its output registers may be jointly entangled and serials need not be distinct. This also applies to k=0. The construction has no ideal oracle, externally supplied setup, obfuscation assumption, leakage assumption, or additional hardness assumption. The target is the implication from the explicitly stated LWE assumption; a construction with an arbitrary computational reduction qualifies.

context_blocks.text: Public-key quantum money requires anyone holding the classical public key to verify a note while preventing a holder of several notes from creating an additional valid one. Reusability makes verification compatible with repeated transfer.

Known constructions with stronger assumptions and restricted impossibility results leave a gap. iO-based schemes and schemes founded on group-action assumptions do not establish the LWE-only implication specified here.
The 2025 obfuscation barrier applies to a particular black-box interface. It is evidence about a restricted class of constructions, not a refutation of this unrestricted implication.

why: Ground publicly verifiable unclonable quantum states in a standard lattice assumption, resolving a central assumption gap in quantum cryptography.

progress.text: The cited construction obtains public-key quantum money using iO together with quantum-hard LWE.
Zhandry proves a restricted black-box obstruction for evasive-obfuscation approaches.
Group-action constructions provide different concrete assumptions rather than LWE alone.

answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with a complete Lean-checked proof covering the specified model and all quantifiers. A restricted model, additional unproved assumption, or partial parameter range does not settle the target.

sentences: Public-key quantum money consists of a classical serial number and a reusable quantum note.
Anyone can verify with the public key, but k honest notes must not enable production of k+1 accepted notes.
This card fixes the decisional LWE parameters and asks for security under that assumption alone.
Existing stronger-assumption constructions and restricted black-box barriers leave this implication unsettled.
A complete answer must preserve both reusable correctness and security against polynomial-size quantum adversaries.
